movie.title: Come and See
movie.overview: The invasion of a village in Belarus by German forces sends young Flyora into the forest to join the weary Resistance fighters, against his family's wishes. There he meets a girl, Glasha, who accompanies him back to his village. On returning home, Flyora finds his family and fellow peasants massacred. His continued survival amidst the brutal debris of war becomes increasingly nightmarish, a battle between despair and hope.

facts: Did you know director Elem Klimov had to fight an incredible eight years of censorship from Soviet authorities just to get 'Come and See' made in its entirety? Talk about a battle for artistic vision!

The film's powerful screenplay wasn't just based on one source, but two significant literary works: the 1971 novel *Khatyn* and the 1977 collection of survivor testimonies titled *I Am from the Fiery Village*.

Adding to its authenticity, one of the film's screenwriters, Ales Adamovich, actually co-authored *I Am from the Fiery Village*, directly connecting him to the real-life survivor accounts that inspired the movie.
